subject: Using recordTable to obtain all records?

messages.author: c1310ae8b03a4683
messages.subject: Using recordTable to obtain all records?
parts:
Juergen

camtrapR's recordTable interrogates the folder of images and the images' metadata and creates the table.  My understanding is that after the first image for the new minute in the Date and Time field further images within the same minute are ignored.

I recognise that longer time intervals can be prescribed. But I ask about 1 second time resolution.

Can you or I relax the one minute interval resolution and have all the images (as small as 1 seconds apart) added to the recordTable?

Thanks

David

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Using recordTable to obtain all records?
parts:
Hi David,
recordTable can return all records, even the ones taken within one minute. Set argument minDeltaTime = 0 (which is the default), then all images which are at least 1 second apart are returned.
Cheers,
Jürgen

messages.author: c1310ae8b03a4683
messages.subject: Re: Using recordTable to obtain all records?
parts:
J
Ah, I see.  There are indeed records with the same station, species, camera and same time (to one second resolution). Although the Reconyx cameras are taking pictures at nominally one second intervals there are occasions when successive pairs of images have exactly the same time stamp in the sets of 3, or 5 or 10 successive images.

As much as one in five. 

Well that solves that anomaly.

Thanks for your careful and thorough documentation.

D

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Using recordTable to obtain all records?
parts: Yes, that's right. Records of the same species at the same station (and camera) taken at exactly the same time are considered duplicates and all but one are removed by default. If you want them in the record table though you can set argument removeDuplicateRecords = FALSE in recordTable.
